In the parable of the great banquet, the master orders his servant, 'go out quickly into the streets' (Luke 14:21). John's Gospel uses it with sharp narrative economy -- Judas leaves the last supper after Jesus says 'what you are going to do, do quickly' (John 13:27). Revelation closes with the promise 'I am coming quickly' (Rev 2:16; 11:14; 22:7, 12, 20). Spanish pronto/rapidamente, French vite, and German schnell converge on one temporal-speed sense."
